translations.text: The vision that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
How long, LORD, must I cry out without you hearing? I cry out to you about violent people, but you do not deliver.
Why have you shown me injustice and [?]? I see plunder and evil before me. A trial took place, and the judge accepted a bribe.
Therefore the law has become powerless, and judgment does not come out justly. Because the wicked treat the righteous very badly, judgment comes out twisted.
Look, you insolent people, and see! Marvel and be astonished, for I am doing a work in your days that you would not believe if someone told you.
For look, I am raising up the Chaldeans, an insolent and bitter nation that marches across the breadth of the earth to take possession of dwellings that are not its own.
He is mighty and fearsome; his judgment comes from himself, and he displays his splendor.
Its horses are swifter than eagles and fiercer than evening wolves. Its horsemen fly; its horsemen come from far away and fly like an eagle hungry for food.
They all come to plunder. Their faces look fierce, and they gather captives like sand.
It mocks kings and scoffs at rulers. It laughs at every fortified city, heaps up earth, and captures it.
Then its spirit will change and pass on, and it will become guilty; its strength is its god.
For you have been from the beginning, LORD my God, the Holy One who does not [?]. You, LORD, appointed him for judgment, and you formed me to rebuke him.
Your eyes are pure and do not look at evil; you cannot look upon wrongdoing. Why do you look upon the insolent and remain silent when the wicked swallow up the righteous?
You have made human beings like the fish in the sea, like crawling creatures that have no ruler.
They all come up on a hook, are dragged in a net, and are gathered in a dragnet. When he has gathered them, he rejoices and exults.
He sacrifices to his net and offers incense to his dragnet, because through them his portion is rich and his food is choice.
Therefore he casts his net continually and kills nations without pity.
I will stand at my post, stationed on a rock, and look out to see what he says to me and what answer he gives me about my complaint.
The LORD answered me and said, “Write the vision and make it plain on tablets, so that whoever reads it may run with it.
For the vision is for its appointed time; the end is coming and will not prove false. If it delays, do not lose heart, for it will come quickly and will not delay.
His soul takes no pleasure in the wicked, but the righteous person will live by faith.
The insolent and greedy man is never satisfied. He has made his appetite as wide as Sheol and, like death, is never satisfied. He gathers all peoples to himself and draws all nations to himself.
All these will take up proverbs, riddles, and taunts against him and say, “Woe to the one who gathers and multiplies for himself what is not his! How long will he heap a cloud of mud upon himself?”
Look, those who bite you will rise suddenly, and those who shake you will awaken, and you will become plunder for them.
Because you plundered many nations, the nations that remain will plunder you, because of human bloodshed and violence against the land, the city, and all its inhabitants.
Woe to the one who oppresses and gathers evil for himself, setting his nest on high to escape evil!
You have devised shame for your house. You have plundered many peoples and brought sin upon yourself.
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the peg in the wood will answer it.
Woe to anyone who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town through injustice!
All these things are from the Lord Almighty: the peoples will be battered by fire, and the nations will exhaust themselves for nothing.
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.
Woe to anyone who makes his companion drink the dregs of your wrath and makes him drunk, so that he may gaze at their nakedness!
You are filled with shame instead of honor. Drink, you too, and stagger! The cup in the Lord’s right hand will come around to you, and shame will cover your honor.
For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the plundering of the animals will terrify you, because of human bloodshed and the violence done to the land, the city, and all its inhabitants.
What benefit has a carved image brought, which its craftsman carved? It is a cast image and a teacher of falsehood, yet its craftsman’s heart has trusted in it, making a speechless idol.
Woe to anyone who says to wood, “Wake up!” and to a speechless stone, “Arise!” They are worthless and covered with gold, and there is no breath in them.
But the Lord is in his holy temple. Let the whole earth tremble before him.
The prayer of Habakkuk the prophet.
Lord, I heard your name and was afraid. Lord, [?] your works in the midst of the years of life; in the midst of the years you will be known. In wrath, remember your mercy.
God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. The heavens were covered by the radiance of the Glorious One, and the earth was filled with his praise.
His brightness will be like light. In the town of his hands [?] he will place his strength in [?].
Death went before him, and pestilence went out at his feet.
He stood and measured the earth; he looked and deceived the nations. The ancient mountains were scattered, and the everlasting hills were brought low. The ancient paths are his.
I saw the tents of Cushan under affliction. The tent curtains of the land of Midian will tremble.
Was the Lord angry with the rivers? Was your anger against the rivers, or your fury against the sea? You rode on your horses and on your chariot of salvation.
Your bow will surely be roused, and the arrows will be satisfied at your glorious command. The earth will be plowed by rivers.
The mountains saw you and trembled. A torrent of water swept past; the deep raised its voice and lifted its hands high.
The sun and moon stood in their dwellings. They travel by the light of your arrows and by the brightness of the flashes of your spears.
In fury you will tread upon the earth, and in anger you will thresh the nations.
You went out to save your people and to save your anointed one. You cut off the head from the house of the wicked and stripped him from his foundations up to his neck forever.
With his own staffs you pierced the heads of his rulers, who trusted in their arrogance to devour the poor in secret.
You trod through the sea on your horses, through the mass of mighty waters.

I heard, and my belly trembled at the utterance of my lips. Trembling entered my bones, and my knees shook, because he announced to me and showed me the day of distress that is coming upon the people.

For the fig tree has not sprouted, and there are no leaves on the vine. The olive’s fruit has failed, and the threshing floors have produced no grain. The sheep have disappeared from the flocks, and there are no cattle in the herds.
But I will rejoice in the Lord and be glad in God my Savior.
The Lord of dominions is my strength. He made my feet like those of a deer and set me upon my heights, so that I may sing his praises.
